newsitem.title: USA: FINA, Holly set product pipeline alliance.
newsitem.headline: FINA, Holly set product pipeline alliance.

text.p: FINA Inc said Monday it had formed an alliance with Holly Corp to create a comprehensive supply network that will provide gasoline and diesel supply to satisfy demand growth in the West Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona markets for at least the next five years.
When fully operational, the system will have the capacity to provide up to 155,000 barrels of refined products per day to these Southwest markets, the Petrofina SA subsidiary said.
The project will use existing assets, FINA said.

Its bi-directional Amdel Pipeline would be converted, when needed, to finished fuels products from crude oil and transport up to 50,000 barrels per day from FINA's Port Arthur, Texas, Refinery on the Gulf Coast, while 45,000 barrels per day will be supplied from FINA's Big Spring, Texas, Refinery.
In addition, Holly's Navajo Refinery in Artesia, N.M., will provide 60,000 barrels per day of fuels products.
FINA said it will construct a 50 mile extension of its Amdel Pipeline from Wink, Texas, to Holly's Pipeline station at Orla, Texas.
A long-term agreement with Holly will enable FINA to transport up to 20,000 barrels per day on Holly's recently expanded 12" pipeline to El Paso.

In New Mexico, Holly will construct a 50 mile pipeline connection from its Artesia Refinery to a recently leased pipeline which will then provide direct service to Albuquerque and the Four Corners area.
FINA said the agreement with Holly will provide product supply along the full extent of this system, from Bloomfield in northwest New Mexico, east to Duncan, Oklahoma, and south to El Paso.

This pipeline system, along with other recently announced El Paso area pipeline expansions, will provide supply to fully use existing common carrier pipelines which ship product from El Paso to New Mexico, Arizona, and Mexico. In addition, the new system will provide FINA access to Mid-Continent refinery products via a reversible product pipeline connecting Big Spring to Wichita Falls.

"Since 95 percentof the pipeline already exists, the system provides the lowest capital cost alternative for product supply from the Gulf Coast to the Southwest markets," said Jeff Morris, vice president of FINA's southwestern unit.

"With our recent acquisition of a 34 percent interest in Southwest Convenience Stores, the nation's largest 7-Eleven franchisee, our West Texas and New Mexico market share is approaching 20 percent, making FINA one of the largest branded marketers in the region," he said.
"This product supply alliance will effectively supply our existing customers, as well as our planned marketing growth."

"This project, as with our previously announced transportation joint venture with MAPCO (Inc ) and Amoco (Corp ), permits Holly to maximize its returns by realizing increased transportation revenues while maintaining ample distribution capabilities for our growing New Mexico refinery production," Holly President Matt Clifton said.

Product terminals owned by the two companies are located in Wichita Falls, Abilene, Big Spring, and El Paso, Texas; Artesia and Albuquerque, N.M.; and Tucson, Ariz. An additional terminal will be purchased or constructed in Bloomfield, N.M., with the potential of an additional terminal in Austin, Texas.
